name: ParkourCheckpoints
description: Build and run multiple independent named parkour courses, each with its own start pad, ordered checkpoints, finish pad, and leaderboard.
usage: Run /parkour create sky, stand where you want the start and type /parkour setstart sky, then setend sky and try it
manual: Operators design courses with /parkour create <name>, then stand on the exact block that should be the start and run /parkour setstart <name>, stand on the finish block and run /parkour setend <name>, and add as many /parkour addcheckpoint <name> blocks as they like along the route (use /parkour clearcheckpoints <name> to wipe them and /parkour delete <name> to remove a course entirely). Anyone can browse courses with /parkour list, see details with /parkour info <name>, check times with /parkour leaderboard <name>, and bail out of a run with /parkour leave. Walking onto a course's start block begins a timed run for that course specifically, its checkpoints save your last-good spot, and reaching its end block finishes the run, records your best time, and shows a firework burst with a completion sound. Falling too low teleports you back to your most recent checkpoint (or the world spawn if you have not started a run) - the min-y setting (default -10) controls how far you can fall before that kicks in. The require-sequential-checkpoints toggle (default on) decides whether checkpoints must be hit in order to count, and leaderboard-size (default 10) controls how many names show per /parkour leaderboard listing. Since every course tracks its own exact block locations, you can build as many overlapping or separate courses as you want without them interfering with each other.
creator: player
